title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes are building, for a morphism X -> Y (with a 'base' T -> X such as a universal cover or a geometric point), a profinite group E^T_{X/Y}. It is the 'relative' or geometric fundamental group of X over Y. On the previous page it was identified as a kernel Ker(pi_1(X) -> pi_1(Y)), computed via universal covers (17-18). Taking T to be a geometric point xi_x gave (19): E^{xi_x}_{X/Y} = pi_1(X_{xi_y}, xi_x), the fundamental group of the geometric fibre.

This page links the two descriptions, referring back to description (11).
- If xi_X comes from a geometric point xi_T of T, there are canonical isomorphisms (20): E^{xi_T}_{X/Y} = E^T_{X/Y} = pi_1(X_{xi_Y}, xi_T).
- Consequently the groups pi_1(X_{xi_Y}, xi_T) of the geometric fibres, indexed by the various geometric points of T, are canonically isomorphic to one another. All of them are identified with the single group E^T_{X/Y}.

Then comes a caveat. E_{X/Y} (without a chosen base) is only a diagram of isomorphisms of profinite groups (a 'transitive system', in the weak sense). It is not an outer group, i.e. not a group defined up to its own inner automorphisms. The ambiguity of the isomorphism E^T_{X/Y} -> E^{T'}_{X/Y} comes from choosing a path (a 'section'/element) in the larger group E^T_X. Conjugation by elements of E_X acts on the normal subgroup E_{X/Y}, and this is not inner to E_{X/Y}.

The next page draws the conclusion. E_X should be seen as an extension of E_Y (the arithmetic, Galois-type group) by E_{X/Y} (the geometric pi). The key case is Y = Spec K, giving 1 -> pi_1(X_{Kbar}) -> pi_1(X) -> Gal(Kbar/K) -> 1 and the outer Galois action on the geometric fundamental group.
errors: No mathematical error. The phrase 'relatifs aux divers pts géom de E^T_{X/Y}' should logically read 'of T' (geometric points of the base T). Either it is a slip or the reading is ambiguous in the image.

The canonicity of the isomorphisms between fibre pi_1's for different points of T relies on T being connected (or simply connected over the relevant part, e.g. a universal cover). That hypothesis is implicit from the previous pages, not restated here.

ideas.what: Identification of the kernel of pi_1(X) -> pi_1(Y) (computed with a base T) with pi_1 of the geometric fibre at a point coming from T
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy exact sequence / geometric fundamental group pi_1(X_{Kbar})
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (exact sequences for fundamental groups); letter to Faltings 1983; Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Using a simply connected 'base' T instead of a point to rigidify fundamental groups, so that fibre groups at different points of T are canonically isomorphic
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with respect to a family of base points / tangential-type base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 groupoids); Deligne 1989 for tangential base points
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V (fundamental groupoid); Esquisse d'un programme (groupoids with many base points)

ideas.what: Remark that the geometric fundamental group without base point is a diagram of isomorphisms, ambiguous up to conjugation by the ambient extension, not an outer group
ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois action G_K -> Out(pi_1^geom); band/lien; group in a gerbe
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), Esquisse d'un programme; Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne for liens

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard foundational bookkeeping page. It identifies the relative fundamental group with the pi_1 of geometric fibres and warns about base-point ambiguity. All of this is SGA1-level material that is well known in anabelian geometry.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: struck word replaced by an insertion that may read 'les compléments' rather than 'description'. The reading is uncertain; the reference '(11)' is correct.
In (20), the left side is E^{xi_T}_{X/Y} and the right side is E^T_{X/Y}. The vertical '≀' leads to pi_1(X_{xi_Y}, xi_T), with xi_Y as a subscript of X.
'[-...-] où les' is likely a struck 'tous' / 'ou' followed by 'où les'.
'(2 mots précis[?])' is probably an inserted '(2 mots précisés)' or similar, written under 'faire attention'.
'au[?] plus' may read 'au plus' ('at most a diagram of isomorphisms of profinite groups'); the reading is plausible.
